utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. No preliminaries, therefore can the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. The Defence now has the B/C/S of the table of contents and it's going into e-court as we speak, and when that happens I can offer the book again into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic is confirming by nodding his head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Gallagher. Perhaps needless to say, but you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony, and Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to start today by referring to one of the videos, the segments that you talked about and that we all viewed last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for purposes of identification, I will call up the Skorpions video but it was identified as part of Exhibit P1147 and is the video labelled V000-9267, the segment going from 01:06:15 to 01:26:12 on the Prosecution's exhibit list. I would like to spend the first part of my examination focusing on that video, and to accompany that I'd like to turn to the stills book, which is P1148 marked for identification, and I'd like to turn to page 153 in the hard copy and page 165 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, Ms. Gallagher, is this image that I have now called up on e-court in fact taken from that same Skorpions video that I have identified which was played last week by Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, according to your information and investigations that you conducted, is it correct that this flag that is depicted here is not a flag of the VRS, that is to say, the Army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a flag of the Skorpion unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And looking at this page from the stills book, at the bottom, the location is indicated to be at the Skorpion headquarters in Djeletovci, Croatia, and is dated the 25th of June, 1995. Does this information that's included in the stills book accord with the information known to you from your investigative work?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The headquarters were located in Djeletovci at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And also from your investigative work, would you agree that the Skorpions were an armed formation primarily active in the area known as the Republic of Serbian Krajina on the territory of the former Yugoslav Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were most of that time, though, with missions to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, as part of your investigative work, can you confirm that the Skorpions were not an armed formation of the VRS, the Army of Republika Srpska, at the time of the Srebrenica operation in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were -- they were subordinated to the MUP, who was subordinated to the VRS in Bosnia at that time, but they were a separate formation prior to the operation and specifically in Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any problems with the sound? If so ... Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And -- I apologise. Did you have a chance to complete your answer?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And one thing that I noticed and probably you have known for some time having probably studied the video longer than I have, but the Skorpion members in that video that we watched last week did not appear to have any VRS emblems or insignia on their uniforms, did they?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek -- let me see. The question -- yes, Mr. Ivetic, you asked -- you described the Skorpions and what kind of a formation it was and that were mainly active in the area known as the Krajina in Croatia. Then your answer I read it from the transcript was: "They were most of that time, though, with missions to Bosnia." Do I understand that you confirm the description of the unit but that you do not confirm that they were mainly active in the Krajina in Croatia? Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say they were mainly posted in the Krajina in Djeletovci area; however, they were sent out on missions to Bosnia. And as we have seen in this Trnovo mission, that's one example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that clarifies your answer. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can focus on the part of the video that was aired last week of the Skorpions personnel killing several individuals, the exhibit list from the Prosecution dates the video as being the 25th of June, 1995. According to your information and investigation, is that in fact the date of the events depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initial where you're seeing this ceremony, the blessing of the Skorpion unit, that is -- that takes place on June 25th, 1995. There's much more to this video than what was shown in court and it chronicles other days, such as throughout the rest of June into early July. And then it's -- of 1995 and then it stops. What we have noted as the dates of the killing clip of the video that you saw was sometime between July 12th and July 24th. We don't know exactly which days the killings happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I think on the next page of the stills book we have that range that you have -- that you have now given for us. And does that mean, then, with respect to the entire investigation that you've performed, you cannot exclude the possibility that the events that occurred on that videotape occurred as late as the 24th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. We -- what we're saying is it happened -- we believe it happened and the evidence that we've -- our team and other teams have gathered through other witnesses and through documents that sometime between the 12th and the 24th it occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now discussing the events that were depicted in that part of the segment that was aired last week, would you confirm for me that the location of those events was at or near Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It's nearby Trnovo in an area called Godinske Bare which is an area of weekend houses a couple of kilometres from Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to make matters clear, Mr. Ivetic, whenever you ask where it was, what happened, et cetera, I take it that you -- the question always is: What did you learn on the basis of your investigations about?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the witness has no direct knowledge of any of these things as I understand you well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, based upon what you know from the basis of your investigations, were the bodies of the victims recovered near Trnovo?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were recovered in the area that you saw on the video inside and nearby the weekend house in Godinske Bare.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, Madam, for those -- if you can help out those of us who have not had the opportunity to do a site visit on the ground, isn't Trnovo closer to Sarajevo than it is to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, to travel from Srebrenica to Trnovo, one would have to either go around Sarajevo or through Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's -- obviously you can get there in several different routes, but that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree, again based upon the knowledge that you've gained from your investigations, that the distance between Srebrenica and Trnovo is approximately 140 to 160 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it's close to that. I don't know if that's -- I believe that it's over a hundred kilometres. I'm not sure about if it's as much as 140 or 160, but it's a significant distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, would you agree with me - again based on your investigative work - that the Skorpions unit was supposed to be engaged on the part of the civilian police authorities near Sarajevo and was tasked with defending against army BiH attacks during the stated time-period when the events in the video occurred?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe they were -- they were subordinated with other MUP units to come and defend Trnovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to the video itself, would you agree with me that this Skorpions video first came to light sometime before -- during the trial of Slobodan Milosevic, that is to say, the early years of 2000?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly know that the time that the OTP became aware of the video is a little later than -- is 2003; however, they didn't first see the video until 2000 -- first acquire the video until 2004, September 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you about the origin of the video, could you tell us how and when it came into the possession of the Office of the Prosecutor in 2004?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can certainly give you a brief synopsis of it. There will be other people, I believe, that will be testifying that can give you more details --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to worry about who will come as a witness. Just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if Mr. Ivetic is happy with a short synopsis, I don't know to what extent you have personal knowledge or what you -- whether it's hearsay, but please don't worry about the course of the proceedings and whether other witnesses will testify. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know that the Sarajevo field office had been approached by somebody who said they had a copy of this video. The field office got in touch with one of the team investigators, Tore Soldal, who then travelled to Sarajevo to meet with this person who had the video and along with Dermot Groome. And they met the intermediary who had the video and were able to watch it and that's initially -- and were able to gain a copy of it. So that's how the OTP first acquired it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now as part of your investigations, you have been unable to locate any indicia that this video was broadcast publicly on TV and at any time during the war, that is to say, during the years of 1995 or even 1996; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not seen any documentation, any statements, that it was ever broadcasted on TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Again, as part of your investigations, you have no evidence that such a video was ever in the possession of or shown to General Mladic prior to last week; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from the coincidental fact that the unfortunate victims in the video hail from Srebrenica, there is not any link between this video and the VRS operating in and around Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I quite understand the question. Can you rephrase it in terms of the link between the video and the VRS operating.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, perhaps it's good to make a distinction between what can be seen on the video and whether there's other information available. Where you ask about: "There is not any link between this video ..." Now, that can be based on information not contained in the video itself or contained in the video. Perhaps it's good to make that distinction. The question remains the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you are invited to rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that the results of your investigative work have -- have been able to determine that the victims depicted in the video originate from the town of Srebrenica or hail from the town of Srebrenica, but that apart from that, there has been no link between the events depicted in the video and the events that were occurring in and around Sarajevo from 13 July -- excuse me, Srebrenica, 13 July through 16 July?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the -- from a witness statement, the witness did say that this was one of several trips that they, the Skorpion unit, made to Srebrenica to collect victims and then to bring them somewhere to have them killed. Aside from that statement and what you see on the video and knowing that the victims are from the Srebrenica area, we don't -- I'm not aware of another link with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And are you aware from your investigative work that the Serbian courts have convicted certain of the Skorpions for this crime in the video and levied the maximum jail sentence available under the law?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, a little bit earlier you mentioned the Skorpion units being subordinated. I would like to ask you as part of your investigative work, have you had an occasion to review the Law on Internal Affairs, particularly Articles 10 and 14 of the same, that were in effect on the territory of Republika Srpska during the stated time-period in 1995?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I'm -- I'm not aware that I'm familiar with these articles, 10 and 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you used the word "resubordinated," did you have in mind the elements of the applicable law that in this case of resubordination, the chain of command is retained by the original unit, that is to say that the chain of command is not transferred to a new chain of command?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the witness just testified that she is not familiar with the legal aspects of this. I think your question is very much focusing on whether the witness had in mind the applicable law which she says she is not familiar with. Unless I misunderstood you, Ms. Gallagher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So then when you say "resubordinated," you don't intend with any kind of legal effect or meaning when you use those terms?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I'm using basically a very similar example regarding the MUP, the RS MUP, being subordinated to the VRS during the Srebrenica operation. And I believe it's a very similar circumstance, so that's -- I'm drawing that same conclusion as to how the RS MUP were subordinated to the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Gallagher, do you use the word "subordinate" in its English meaning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to move along to another topic that is another segment of the Srebrenica trial video that we viewed last week, and this is identified as V000-9268, the segment running from 00:28:27 to 00:33:26 and is related to the Zepa region. Now, last week at transcript page 10.123, you testified that this was some kind of picnic. Would it refresh your recollection to be told that this was, in fact, a physical fitness test conducted of the entire VRS Main Staff that involved a hike on foot from Han Pijesak to Zepa?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of watching the raw footage of it, I wouldn't have characterised it as a physical fitness test, but I know that they were -- that they did do a long hike.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, that long hike occurred in June of 1996, essentially a full year after the military action in Srebrenica and Zepa had been completed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now still at transcript page 10.123, last week you were saying at line 13 that General Mladic was pointing out some of the historical and important places during the war, in fact viewing the entire footage of this segment. Would it be, in fact, accurate to say that he was also chronicling atrocities committed by the Muslim forces in places against Serb civilians and soldiers and in fact attacks against himself?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he's pointing -- if my memory is correct, he's pointing out some of the battle sites, some of the areas they lost, some of the areas they won, some of the key towns, some of the key sort of locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Churches and villages that had been razed by the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's -- I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I also correct that through the entirety of that video segment, it's not just General Mladic giving background on the historical context of various locations but also other persons are seen doing the same through this video?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. He's not -- as I remember, he's not the only person that's speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There was another video segment shown last week which was identified as follows: V000-9266 and the segment was identified as running from 00:32:29 to 00:44:52 and is labelled the Zivanovic speech. And just to make sure that we are all on the same page about what I am referring to, let's look at the Srebrenica stills book, again P1148, MFI, and it will be at page 85 in e-court, page 73 in the hard copy. And this is identified as a St. Peter and Paul patron day, 12 July 1995. And if we can turn to the next page in both versions of the book, we can see a still taken from this video so that we can place it in our memories from last week.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And first of all, Ms. Gallagher, am I correct that from a review of this footage in total, General Mladic does not appear to be present for this event.

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's not present.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that this appears to be a private gathering and event at the home of Mr. Bajagic and, indeed, appears to be his patron saint's day or Slava?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And does it also appear that it is a civilian gathering where civilians and, indeed, children are present?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- I recall it's a mix of some military members, civilians, as you can see what -- there's staff that are waiting on them. And yes, I think there must be several children.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've identified some military members. Am I correct from a review of the entire segment that apart from Mr. Zivanovic, Mr. Bajagic and about two other persons in army uniform that I saw, the vast majority of the people present are clearly civilians, dressed in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly most of the people gathered there are wearing civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that there are not any members of the VRS Main Staff visible as being present at this celebration?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now what about the results of your investigation and what you know from there, can you confirm that the results from your investigation have indicated that neither General Mladic nor anyone else from the VRS Main Staff was present on this occasion at this event?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that question not yet put and answered?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd asked her if they were visible on the video and now I'm asking about, in addition to what's physically seen on the video, if her investigation can confirm that neither General Mladic or the VRS Main Staff were present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the answers, perhaps, went a bit beyond your question, that is that -- who was not present. But there's no major problem in answering this question whether for the first time or again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. There doesn't appear -- and as far as I know no other -- no one else from the Main Staff that was present at this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. Now, this celebration of Mr. Bajagic who, according to this page that we have up in e-court now from the book, in addition to being the clerk of the technical services detachment of the Drina Corps is also a curator of St. Peter's church. Is this information contained in the book the result of your investigation and what that showed?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. He does wear other hats as well, but those were two more official roles he plays.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you, Ms. Gallagher, the bottom of these pages relating to this video segment identify this particular video coming from the Mladic seizure footage. Can you tell us when this video came to the Prosecution's possession?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was a search and seizure done of the Mladic family home. There were two conducted, one in 2008, one in 2010. I believe this is the 2008 search and seizure of his home in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, prior to 2008, the Mladic household in Belgrade had been searched multiple occasions without this video having been found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, in 2008, based on your information, General Mladic was no longer residing at the Mladic residence in Belgrade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you cannot exclude the possibility that this video came to be -- came to arrive at the -- at that location at some time after General Mladic had vacated the premises, can you?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I can't exclude any possibility, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Has your investigation revealed that other people cohabitated in that household and, indeed, continued to reside on the premises after General Mladic was no longer living there?

utterances.speaker: ERIN GALLAGHER [Resumed]
utterances.text: His wife has resided there and had been residing there, so I'm -- I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask a few clarifying questions. Mr. Ivetic referred to multiple searches at multiple occasions before 2008. They were conducted by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of these searches have been conducted by the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say "most of them." The others were conducted by ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I -- I want to be careful. I don't want to say that they all have been because I don't know the history of all the searches. I know for sure 2008 and 2010 were conducted by the Serbian MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And were you involved or had you requested in any way for these prior searches before 2008? Mr. Ivetic, no loud speaking from Mr. Mladic and to remain seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have -- do you know where exactly the -- this video was found during the search?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's found in the home, but I'm a little more familiar with the second search. I'm not -- I don't recall where exactly, if it's a bookcase, a cupboard, or a bedroom. That part I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask a follow-up question as to the searches --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'd forgotten that due to the interruption that you had not answered my question about whether there was any involvement from the OTP in the early searches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That I don't know. I know in 2008, 2010, it did not come upon the request of the OTP. We were alerted when the searches happened and I don't know prior -- or the OTP involvement prior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge of the procedures and protocols that have been in place for investigations being conducted, would it have been expected procedure that at least for some of these searches that had been conducted at the request of the OTP or the Tribunal, that representatives of the Tribunal would have been present when Serbian officials conducted a search of the premises?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have some confusion. I may have misunderstood your answers. I did understand your answers to be that in 2008 and 2010 the searches were not conducted at the request and you do not know for the earlier searches. So therefore, Mr. Ivetic, I'm a bit confused by your reference to the searches at the request of --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I had not caught that last half as to the -- I had only heard that the 2008 and 2010 were not -- I stand corrected and therefore withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I'd like to look at another segment of the trial video that we viewed which was identified on the exhibit list as being video V000-9266 from 00:00:17 to 00:01:19, a body in Srebrenica town 12 July 1995. Now, at transcript page 10.116 last week, you talked about this clip where there is a body visible on the screen and you said that Drazen Erdemovic described how this man had died in the Tolimir trial; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's one decision to be read in open session and one in private session. I'll start with the decision on the admission of Exhibits P957 and P958 into evidence. On the 14th of January, 2013, the Prosecution filed a Rule 92 ter motion tendering transcript excerpts from witness Edin Suljic's previous testimony in the Galic case. On the 28th of January, the Defence responded submitting that portions of the tendered transcripts amounted to hearsay and expert evidence and should therefore be redacted. On the 14th of February, in the course of the witness's testimony, these transcript excerpts were marked for identification as P957. Also during the course of the witness's testimony, the Prosecution tendered a report containing what Suljic described as expert opinion upon which he relied during his investigation. The Defence also objected to the admission of this report on the basis that it was improperly tendered expert evidence, citing as support decision from the Milutinovic et al. and the Lukic and Lukic cases. The report was marked for identification as P958. On the 14th and 15th of February, the Defence made additional objections to the admission of P957 on the grounds that the Prosecution had selected only portions of the previous testimony which had not been translated into B/C/S, thereby undermining the accused's ability to prepare for this witness's cross-examination, and that these excerpts included mistakes later identified by the witness. With regard to the Defence's objection concerning the expert nature of the witness's previous testimony, P957, the Chamber recalls its discussion at transcript pages 8730 to 8731 and again notes that, rather than offering an expert opinion, the witness testified about his personal knowledge of and participation in an investigation which included his co-operation with certain experts. With regard to the Defence's objection as to the expert nature of the report marked as P958, the Chamber recalls its discussion at transcript page 8712 and again notes the distinction between expert reports drafted for the purpose of the Tribunal and subject to the procedural requirements of Rule 94 bis as compared to expert reports drafted for other purposes. The Chamber further notes that the case law cited by the Defence does not support the contention that P958 is a statement or report of an expert witness subject to Rule 94 bis. Rather, the cited decisions as well as the jurisprudence of the Appeals Chamber make the same distinction between reports of expert witnesses prepared for the purposes of litigation before the Tribunal and reports containing statements made by non-witnesses for other purposes. The jurisprudence clearly states that the latter type of reports, such as P958, are admissible pursuant to Rule 89(C). The Chamber finds that although the witness's evidence incorporates the expert opinion of others, neither the witness's previous testimony, P957, nor the report about which he testified, P958, can be accurately characterised as a report of an expert witness for the purpose of litigation before the Tribunal. The Chamber does, of course, recognise that portions of P957 and the entirety of P958 constitute hearsay evidence. However, the Chamber again notes that the hearsay nature of evidence does not act as a bar to admission. With regard to the Defence's objection on the basis of there not being a B/C/S transcript of the witness's previous testimony available for the accused, the Chamber notes that the accused has access to the B/C/S audio which the Chamber considers sufficient. With regard to the Defence's objection on the grounds that the witness's previous testimony contains errors in transcription or translation, the Chamber notes that the witness corrected a portion of his previous testimony at transcript pages 8772 to 8773. The Chamber does not find that such errors reduce the reliability of the testimony to such an extent that it becomes inadmissible. Lastly, with regard to the Defence's objection to the Prosecution's selection of transcript excerpts, the Chamber notes that the plain language of Rules 89 and 92 ter clearly permit the admission of portions of a witness's previous testimony and that according to the practice established in this trial the Defence was invited to tender additional portions of the previous testimony but did not do so. For the foregoing reasons, the Chamber denies the Defence request to redact portions of P957 and admits P957 and P958 into evidence. Then we move briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could I clarify one matter, please, Mr. Jeremy. You said 17th February 1998, but I see here the dates 11, 12, and 17th of July, 1995, and it should read 1998? Please clarify the difference between July and February.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I would now propose reading a short summary of this witness's evidence, the purpose of which I have explained to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: From January 1995 to July 1995, Evert Rave was a sergeant-major in the Royal Dutch Army assigned to the Dutch elements of the United Nations Protection Force based in the Srebrenica enclave. On 11 July 1995, Rave was in Srebrenica town the morning the enclave fell. He travelled with the refugees to the UN base in Potocari on the afternoon of the 11th of July, 1995. That evening, Rave attended two meetings at the Hotel Fontana in Bratunac. For the first meeting, Rave travelled together with Colonel Karremans and Major Boering to the Hotel Fontana, arriving at 8.00 p.m. There, General Mladic first spoke of the NATO air-strikes and threatened that if there were any more air-strikes he would respond by shelling the UN compound, killing the Dutch hostages. General Mladic instructed Colonel Karremans to return to the Hotel Fontana at 10:30 p.m. that evening together with Muslim military and civilian representatives. The meeting lasted approximately 30 minutes. Lieutenant-Colonel Kosoric and Captain Momir Nikolic were present at the meeting together with a number of other officers from the Army of Republika Srpska. For the second meeting, Rave travelled to the Hotel Fontana with Colonel Karremans, Major Boering, and Nesib Mandzic, a Muslim civilian representative, arriving at 10.30 p.m. During this meeting, General Mladic talked to Nesib Mandzic about the civilian population and the Muslim military, saying, among other things, that the civilian population was free to go and the military should lay down their weapons. This meeting ended at approximately midnight. Rave remained in Potocari on 12 July 1995 and did not attend the third meeting at the Hotel Fontana on the morning of the 12th of July. He observed the separation and forcible transfer of the civilian population on 12 and 13 July 1995. Throughout this process, he saw men being separated from their families, personal belongings being placed in holding areas. That concludes the summary, Your Honours, and with your leave, I now propose to ask the witness some additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, before we begin, I see you have some materials in front of you. Could you briefly explain to the Court what these are?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, I brought some notebooks and a diary which I used during the whole period and especially also in the last days in the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Rave, my questions today will be focused on events in the enclave between 10 to the 13th of July, 1995, and also on the 21st of July, 1995. So first let's go to the 10th of July, 1995, and do you recall whether you were in Srebrenica on that day?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: On the 10th of July, I travelled frequently between Srebrenica and Potocari, so I was in both the compounds and in the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: In preparation for your testimony today, do you recall being shown footage of people crowded outside of the Bravo Company compound in Srebrenica on the 10th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll now ask Ms. Stewart to play a short portion of the Srebrenica trial video, 65 ter 28780. Time code 7 minutes, 45 seconds, to 8 minutes, 19 seconds of section V000-9265.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's P1147, Mr. Jeremy?

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we stopped at 8 minutes, 19 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, firstly can you tell us the building that is depicted in this clip?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: That is the UN compound in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And on the 10th of July, 1995, were you aware of any refugees inside of that UN compound?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: On the 10th, we had no refugees inside of the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We saw on the subtitles to the clip that there were shouts to block the road. Can you relate these comments to your own personal experience in Srebrenica on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, on the 10th of July, a lot of people were gathered in front of the UN compound. All those people were very afraid that the UN would leave the compound and go, for example, to Potocari and they wanted to -- that Bravo Company that was in the compound, that they stayed in Srebrenica because for them that was the only safe place to go, and they had the imagination that if the UN would leave Srebrenica, it would be very worse for them. Interesting is that on the night of the 10th and the 11th, we had a meeting in the PTT building with Colonel Karremans and the civilian and military leaders in the enclave, and at that night, we had to pass some trees that they put on the road to block the road and we could with our jeep pass by. But very -- it was very overcrowded, but they really blocked the road to protect themselves and to let the UN stay in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Moving to the 11th of July, 1995, in paragraph 18 of your statement now in evidence as P1149, e-court page 4, you state that on the 11th of July, 1995, Major Boering and yourself departed the Bravo Company compound for Potocari driving in a jeep full of refugees at about 1500 hours. Can you briefly describe the events that led up to your departure from the Bravo Company compound to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, then we have to go back to the night of the 10th. On the 11th -- I think, because at that moment Colonel Karremans informed the military and the civilian leaders that if the VRS was still attacking next morning the town of Srebrenica, there would be an air attack and close air support to support our troops. When the UN was attacked and Srebrenica was attacked, those air-strikes should take place. The next morning, the commander of the Bravo Company sent forward some APCs to check if the VRS was still attacking the town of Srebrenica. Well, that happened. Tank rounds were fired towards our APCs, so we had, I think around 5.00 or 6.00 in the morning, confirmation that the VRS was still attacking the town of Srebrenica and also the UN. At that moment I think there was a request for close air support or maybe an air-strike. I really don't know exactly what Colonel Karremans asked for. And -- but at least nothing happened. I can remember that during that morning it was several times there was a contact with the higher level in Tuzla and maybe also in Sarajevo to get support to stop the VRS going forward to the town of Srebrenica, but nothing happened. Then in the morning from the 11th, there was a very tense situation. The ICRC and the MSF asked us to help evacuate the hospital in Srebrenica. Well, we had no possibilities at all, but we prepared some [indiscernible] on the compound of the Bravo Company that if it was possible to get wounded people from the hospital to the Bravo Company --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, of course. Thanks. Maybe we could evacuate the wounded from the hospital via the Bravo Company to the compound of Potocari where was our own medical facility. During that morning, some wounded of the hospital managed to come to the compound and to get into some trucks we separated. The population of the town of Srebrenica tried to get on the compound because that was for them the only safe place, and all the time a lot of shelling was going on in the town. At the end of --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: So you mentioned that the population tried to get into the compound on the 11th. Were they able to do that?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: First, yes, but there were only a few people. We managed to get them off the compound again, but after I think an hour or maybe an hour and a half, they broke through the fence and came on the compound at, I think, the end of the morning, so around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you mentioned shelling around the compound. Were there any particular shells that you recall?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, there was frequent shelling around the compound, but when the refugees broke through the fence and were on the compound, we had a big problem, of course, because we had no freedom of movement anymore. The compound was overcrowded, and at that moment a mortar shell landed between two APCs on the compound and we had some new casualties among the local people, and we were able to bring some of them inside the UN facility on that compound to give them medical treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, can you briefly explain what we saw in that clip?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: I don't know exactly what time it was, but when the refugees broke through the fence, they entered the compound and also went on the trucks that were on the compound to get the -- because they had the idea when the UN is leaving, then we're leaving with them. And -- well, everybody tried to get on that truck. I think at that moment we already decided - and we, that I mean the commander of the Bravo Company Mr. Boering and myself - that it was a situation that could not take too long on the Bravo Company because we had no freedom of movement. We couldn't do anything for them. The shelling in town was going on, so the best option for us was to try to get the people in the direction of Potocari because we also had a compound over there that was much bigger, we had more facilities, and we tried to get people in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll now ask Ms. Stewart to play another clip again from P1147, time code 15 minutes, 24 seconds, to 16 minutes, 19 seconds, again of section V000-9265.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we've stopped there at 16 minutes, 20 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, in a couple of sentences, could you describe what we saw in that clip, please?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: In this clip we can see that the overcrowded trucks from Srebrenica came to the compound in Potocari. You can see the trucks driving on the compound in Potocari and then going into the factory, where the refugees stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: In paragraph 18 of your statement - that's e-court page 4 - you described the journey to Potocari and you referred to mortar fire originating from VRS positions. You described this as "a deliberate attempt to steer the refugees towards Potocari." Can you please elaborate just a little on how you believe these refugees were being steered towards Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: When we managed - after we had air-strikes at that 2.00 or something like that - to get the stream of refugees in the northern direction, in the direction of Potocari, then there still was mortar fire in that direction. There's only one big road from Srebrenica to Potocari, and on both sides of the road there landed mortar shells. And in my opinion, it was just to take care that -- there was shelling in Srebrenica, there was shelling on both sides of the road, and in that way they tried to steer the refugee stream in the northern direction of Potocari. And I think that what also is important, when I remember well, when we arrived in Potocari, north of the compound in Potocari there also was shelling between the compound in Potocari and Yellow Bridge, so the -- in the direction of Bratunac. So in my opinion, they would not allow that refugees went further than Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'll now move to the evening of the 11th of July, and in particular your -- the meetings that you attended at Hotel Fontana. The first one was at approximately 8.00 p.m. on the 11th, and you discussed this in paragraphs 23 to 28 of your statement, e-court pages 5 to 6. In particular, in paragraph 25 of your statement you state that: During the early part of the meeting, "General Mladic remained upset, and for a few minutes I wondered if we would be taken outside and shot." I don't propose to play any of this footage again. The Court has seen a fair proportion of it, but could you please explain why you felt you might be taken outside and shot at that time?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, in the first place we didn't expect to see General Mladic over there. We had no interpreter at that moment, so the beginning of the conversation was also a little bit difficult. Colonel Jankovic was used as an interpreter. After that, Petar, the interpreter came in, and the way General Mladic started to examine in this -- first Colonel Karremans, afterwards Major Boering and myself, about if we were -- we were the ones who asked for the air-strikes, if we were responsible for killing his soldiers. There were a lot of other threats, of course, that if there were other air-strikes he would target the compound. He would kill our hostages [sic]. He suggested that, offering a cigarette to Colonel Karremans - I didn't smoke at that moment - "It will not be your last cigarette. Do you want to see your family or your child and children again? We were happy here before you came and now not any longer. You've only one life, you don't want to lose it over here." All those kind of threats in the first ten minutes, and especially because we didn't know what to expect, that was rather tense. After that, it faded away a little bit because then we got the impression that not we were the targets but the Muslim population then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd now like to take you to the second meeting at Hotel Fontana that you attended on the same evening of the 11th of July and which you discuss in paragraphs 29 to 34 of your statement, e-court pages 6 and 7. In particular, in paragraph 30 you describe an incident during which a pig was slaughtered outside an open window. You state in particular that in your opinion the incident was staged. Can you please elaborate a little on why you believe that this incident was staged?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: When we arrived over there we sat down. The meeting started and I took some notes, and the meeting started at 11.00. At five minutes past 11.00 somebody - and I think it was a soldier - was standing near the window and the curtains. He opened the curtain, he opens a window, and under that window, in my opinion, a pig was slaughtered. I looked around and I saw no amazing faces at all. The only thing I saw that Kosoric, who was sitting opposite me, was grinsing [phoen]. After - and I don't know exactly how much time it took - and I think I said it might be two but it might also be three or four minutes, the screaming of the pig faded away. Then the soldier closed the window, shut the curtains, and disappeared again. And there was no reaction at all from anybody. And in my opinion, it was pure intimidation by slaughtering a pig and then giving the impression: Well, what happens over there could also happen to you. And then not I think towards the UN but more towards the Muslim representative that was with us, Mr. Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Just to clarify, you said you looked around and you -- you said: "I looked around and I saw no amazing faces at all." What did you mean specifically by that?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, when you open in a rather small vicinity a window, hear a pig screaming when it's slaughtered, and it was a terrible screaming, then somebody should be amazed and somebody should look around and somebody should ask: What's going on? But nobody reacted at all. So I think in my opinion it was all preset and it was -- belonged to the show.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Paragraph 31 of your statement you state that, among others, Colonel Jankovic and Major Nikolic were present at this second meeting. How were you able to recognise, to identify, each of these men?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, Major Nikolic, we dealt with him from the first moment on we came into the enclave, so from the beginning of January. And Colonel Jankovic, I don't know if he was introduced by name in the first meeting or maybe in the second meeting, but of course when this statement was made, I knew Colonel Jankovic rather well, I think, because I met him during the period of the deportation of the local population several times and it was, for me, an easy name to remember. And I don't know if I heard the name on the first, the second -- or the second meeting because I think on the second meeting some other representatives were presented by name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: I'd now like to take you to the 12th of July, 1995, and I'd like to focus your attention on the events during that morning. In paragraph 36 of your statement, e-court page 7, you state that: "In the morning of the 12th, Serbian infantry advanced from the north towards Potocari." And in paragraph 37 you state that Major Franken placed DutchBat soldiers around the DutchBat compound. In connection with this I'd like to show you some footage, some video footage, you were shown in preparation for your testimony today.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'll ask Ms. Stewart to play a couple of minutes of footage from Exhibit P1147, time code 3 minutes, 8 seconds, to 5 minutes, 27 seconds, and that's from section V000-9266.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And we finish there at 5 minutes, 27 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, did you recognise where this conversation that we just saw in the video took place?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, it was on the road from Potocari towards Bratunac, the north-western fence of the UN compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And does this -- does what we saw in this footage relate to your own experience on the morning of the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, I've not been in this situation because I was inside of the compound, but it fits in the total picture that happened that morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Staying with the morning of the 12th of July, I'd like to talk about your -- talk to you about the organisation of the buses in Potocari. And in paragraphs 38 and 39 of your statement, P1149, and that's e-court page 7 in the English and 8 in the B/C/S, you describe how after Colonel Karremans and Major Boering returned from the Hotel Fontana meeting on the morning of the 12th of July, you and Boering went to Bratunac to "sort out the problem of fuel and buses." You then returned to Potocari after being told by Lieutenant Kosoric and Nikolic that the buses were already in Potocari. On arriving back in Potocari, you found that the buses were already there by 1300 hours. At this point, what information did you learn about the organisation of these buses?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, because nothing really substantial was discussed in the meeting of the morning, Major Boering and myself went to Bratunac and tried to find somebody who could tell us what was arranged because it wasn't clear for nobody. At the end, near the Hotel Fontana, Nikolic and Kosoric showed up and told us to go back because buses were already there and there was no discussion anymore. We went back. And when we left nothing was over there, and then when we returned after, I think, half an hour, three-quarters of an hour, the buses were standing in front of the compound. And, well, in my opinion, it was all well arranged and, although Mr. Mladic asked several times to Colonel Karremans if he was able to arrange buses, he already had arranged them themselves. And also the question about the fuel, we didn't get the question again about the fuel. They had the buses and they had the fuel. So it was very well arranged in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Do you recall how many buses were -- you found in Potocari that day?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: I don't know when we returned if it were only buses, but I think it were buses and trucks and approximately 15 standing in front of the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Moving to the afternoon of the 12th of July and also the 13th of July, 1995, in paragraphs 39 to 50 of your statement, e-court pages 7 to 10 in the English and 8 to 10 in the B/C/S, you describe your observations on the separation of the male Muslims from their families in Potocari, and you talk about what you describe as their deportation during the 12th and the 13th of July, 1995. During this time, you described seeing General Mladic in the afternoon of the 12th of July, 1995, and in paragraph 48 of your statement, e-court page 9 in the English, 10 in the B/C/S, you referred to a conversation with Mladic on the 13th of July, 1995. Can you provide the Court with a little more detail about the contents of the conversation or conversations you had with General Mladic over this period?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yeah, I think it was on the 12th when at that time General Mladic went to the refugees and provided them with food. Of course, he was there with a camera crew who filmed everything. All the time -- no, not all the time. He was there for a long time, and we had the refugees on the compound and we had refugees near the bus station. There were two separate locations and people were not able to move from one location to the other one. At one moment I was asked by a mother - and I don't know if she was either on the compound or near the bus station - but her son from, I think, 12 years old was on the other location and she would like to be brought together with her son and asked me if it was possible for me to arrange it. At that moment, General Mladic was around and I asked him if it was possible to bring, I think, the guy to his mother, and, well, that was no problem at all so from one location I took the boy and brought him to his mother. I think at that moment all the time when I was around because our interpreters from the compound didn't dare to leave the compound, we used Colonel Jankovic as an interpreter. So when we had questions for Mr. Mladic at that moment, I asked Colonel Jankovic if he was able to translate it. I think it was on the 13th that I had the question with General Mladic at that moment about our equipment. Lots of soldiers were threatened to hand over their flak jackets, their weapons and other equipment, and I asked him if he was able to stop those things. Well, of course, his answer was that he would try to stop it, but also, of course, nothing happened. When I asked him - because at that moment separation from children and women and elderly men and the -- no, not elderly men, the men between 17 and 60, 65, I think, were separated and brought into the white house. On my question where they were brought to, because they were brought away in separate buses, General Mladic told me that those men were brought to Bijeljina. There was a big prisoner camp in Bijeljina and possibly they would be exchanged for Serbian prisoners that remained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one question to you, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the beginning of this lengthy answer you said: "I think it was on the 12th when at that time General Mladic went to the refugees and provided them with food." Can you explain that a little bit further? What kind of food? What amount of food? Did he do that personally or did he order that? How was that done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I remember well, it was before the buses were there but it also could have been when buses were already there, and General Mladic and at least a body-guard, a film crew, and some other Serbian soldiers went to the blocking positions that we arranged near the bus station and there he provided the refugees with bread and I think with some chocolate, but not in big amounts and it only happened when the camera crew was there. The camera crew at one moment disappeared, General Mladic disappeared, and then it stopped. So it was, in my opinion, only a show to show that he was taking care of the refugees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And you mentioned in your answer that you had a discussion with General Mladic about the separations that were taking place. Were the actual -- were separations actually taking place while Mladic was there at the location of the compound in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yes, because General Mladic was there on the 12th and the 13th, and all the time when buses drove up and down and refugees went into the buses, men walked to the other side of the buses and were separated. So the separation and the filling up of the buses was a continuing story.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, I'll move now to the 21st of July, 1995, and I'll conclude my examination with a question or two about your departure from the enclave on the 21st. In paragraph 62 of your statement, P1149, e-court page 12, you refer to two photos taken at the border of the Republika Srpska and Serbia. And you mention specifically Mladic, Jankovic, and Petar in those photos. For clarity, I'd like to show you those photos now so that you are able to identify those men because a number of other additional men also appear in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremy, does my recollection serve me well that you still need them to be added to the -- that you --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: That's -- that's correct, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: -- and I'd like to take this opportunity to ask if they can be added to the exhibit list .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, any objections against the adding of the two photographs to the 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then leave is granted to add them to the 65 ter list. If you call them to the screen, then Madam Registrar will know which 65 -- they have no 65 ter numbers yet because -- they do provisionally because --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: We provisionally assigned 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You provisionally assigned -- could you use those numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'd like the court officer to please show in e-court 65 ter 28756.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's Exhibit P1132.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Forgive me, I've read out the wrong 65 ter number. It's 65 ter 28790.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, in your statement you identify three men in this photo. You refer to General Mladic, Petar, and Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could be assisted so that he's able to mark the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Rave, I'd like you to mark a number 1 next to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: This is General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Could you place a 1 there, please.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And a 2 next to Petar.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And earlier in your testimony you referred to him as an interpreter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And if you could identify Jankovic in that photo, please.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: With a number 3.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And there's also a second paragraph that's part of the same exhibit on the next e-court page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But once we get it off the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- then the markings will be lost. I suggest that you tender them separately, but the photograph now marked by the witness of which the 65 ter number was given a second ago, Madam Registrar, would receive ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number P1150, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P11150 is admitted into evidence -- I make a mistake. I apologise. Yes, it is 1150 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And could we go to the second photograph that's part of 65 ter 28790, the second page in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And again, Mr. Rave, using the same numbering, if you can identify General Mladic with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: It doesn't work at this moment. Mr. Mladic, 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Petar with a 2.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Petar, 2, and Jankovic is 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd like to tender that photograph as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document marked by the witness receives number P1151, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1151 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, that concludes my direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Jeremy. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am ready, Your Honour. I just need half a minute to organise myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, Mr. Rave, you'll -- after half a minute you'll be cross-examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic and you'll find him to your left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Rave.

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just as my learned friend, I will start from the 10th of July, 1995. Did you hear that on that day, in the evening hours, a conflict broke out between members of the BH army -- or rather, among members of the BH army itself which resulted in casualties, both people dead and killed -- wounded?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 1D887 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your evidence in the Tolimir case on the 27th of October, 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need page 32 in e-court. That should correspond to transcript page 6849. We need lines 11 through 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There you were asked - and I'll read it in English so that you get it correctly interpreted - I'll read in English. [In English] I quote: "'On Monday, 10th July, the commander of OP-M received orders from the C-Company commander to co-ordinate with the BiH army. That same evening, fighting broke out among the BiH army soldiers, resulting in dead and wounded.'" Then line 16 to 18, I quote: "'When the two BiH army soldiers with the anti-tank weapons attempted to prevent their departure, they were shot in the head by the BiH army leader.'" And we can find your answer in lines 22 to 23, when you said: "The only thing I know about this incident is approximately what is stated in this debriefing ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I think it would be fair if you could indicate the origin of the quotation you have put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it's D20 in Tolimir case, but we were not able to locate the very document since we have some problems with the electronics. And I had to quote from the transcript, from the Tolimir trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At least it is stated --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At least it is stated in lines 4 and 5 that: "This is a report based on a debriefing which says, amongst other things ..." and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will clarify this with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Evert, you are aware of the fact that the debriefing took place based on what DutchBat soldiers who were in Srebrenica had to say; right?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yes, a debriefing took place, but I can't imagine that in my debriefing I stated this. One thing that rings a bell is that somebody was shot in the head and that one of the DutchBat soldiers was aware of this and he reported it. But I don't think I reported this in my debriefings. It might be from a debriefing from another DutchBat soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the record --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted say for the record, it's Mr. Rave not Mr. Evert, number 1. Number two, I think if you could make clear that, in fact, this debriefing is not a debriefing of the witness but he was being read this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that should be clarified at least. It should be perfectly clear what you put to the witness, whether you put to him what is his own words or whether it's someone else's words. If the Prosecution could assist in any way to get hold of the debriefing report and the actual -- one second. I'm ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Madam Registrar suggests that she might be able to assist the parties. Something is on our screen now which -- I don't know provided by whom at this very moment but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Madam Registrar has located this report, Mr. Jeremy, Mr. Lukic, and if you would like to use that, if you have got the page reference, but I think in the Tolimir it refers to paragraph 3.58. If you would like to -- Mr. Jeremy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JEREMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Ms. Stewart tells me that the document that Madam Registrar identified is on our 65 ter exhibit list as 17353.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Lukic, if you would like to use that, it is on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. Just say yes and then you will be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that I'm finished, actually, with this document. I just have this introductory question, but I will clarify what you -- Your Honours think that I should clarify with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's do that on the basis of the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- has been referred to in the Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then can we have in the e-court 17353, but since I didn't have this document in my hands, I don't know on which page this paragraph is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is paragraph 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- .58. I take it that it is a ... 3.58 is to be found on -- beginning on e-court page 38. Was this 3.58? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Rave, did you have an opportunity to read the paragraph? And does this refresh your memory, in fact, that at the time you did hear that one of your colleagues reported this incident?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: I think when we returned, that in August the debriefing of all DutchBat soldiers started and, in my opinion, this is paragraph on a summary of all the debriefings. So I don't remember anything more than I told you. And one of the soldiers might have told this in his debriefing, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think it's clear it does not appear as a quote from this witness in paragraph 3.58 in this report. I think that is what we wanted to know for sure and it has been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I think it's time for our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it indeed is. We will take a break and we resume after the witness has left the courtroom, and he's invited to follow the usher, and we will resume after that at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Rave, could we -- can we go on now?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yes, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Immediately preceding the 10th of July, do you know that members of the BH army opened fire on Serb positions wearing blue caps and therefore looking like UNPROFOR members?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: I know that some fights were going on between the BiH and the VRS soldiers, but I'm not aware that BiH soldiers wore blue caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reports at the time that members of the BH army opened fire on Republika Srpska army positions from the vicinity, from the immediate surroundings, of the observation post of the DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: When the VRS started to attack the enclave, BiH soldiers went to the vicinities of the UN OPs, opened fire towards the VRS, and tried to involve the UN in the fights towards the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive reports that members of the 28th Division of the BH army opened fire from the town of Srebrenica itself in those days?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: No. The only thing I know is that the VRS opened fire towards the town of Srebrenica especially with tanks, mortars, and other heavy weapons and not the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were in Srebrenica on the 10th of July, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now, with Ms. Stewart's assistance, see 65 ter -- or, in fact, today it's become an exhibit already, a Prosecution exhibit, P1147, more specifically the section V000-9265. That is a video-clip beginning at 5 minutes, 25 seconds, through 6 minutes, 35 seconds. This is a video-clip that was made by a Muslim from Srebrenica and we will now have a chance to see this 1 minute and 10 seconds. Can we please play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank Ms. Stewart for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This video-clip was presented by the Prosecution as having been made on the 10th of July, 1995. Are you familiar with the location where this petrol station is in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Yes, I know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far was your Bravo Company and your compound from this petrol station in Srebrenica? So what is the distance between Bravo 4 and the petrol station?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: Well, I can't exactly say what the distance was, but it's not too far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But is that by a couple of hundred metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A couple of kilometres? I mean, "not too far" is a relative concept.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not more than a couple of hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And "a couple" means anything between 200 and ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would say between 3- and 700 metres, but I even don't know exactly -- I know the spot, but if it was north of the compound of the Bravo Company or south of it, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you determine which direction this mortar was fired in based on the position of the mortar itself?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: As far as I see it now, they are firing in the southern direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The civilians that we see in the video-clip and that you saw in Srebrenica on that day, did they show any desire to leave Srebrenica or was it rather that they were organised in some way by someone or forced, even, to do so?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
utterances.text: During the day I saw a lot of civilians in the town of Srebrenica just running around, staying in the town of Srebrenica and not knowing where to go. In the evening of the 10th, when we went to the PTT building, we had to pass a crossroad that was a dirt road in the north-western direction. There we saw a huge column of Muslim men from which a lot of them were military uniforms going in the north-western direction. But for the rest, on the day itself, it was unorganised and people were just running around and trying to find a safe spot for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now briefly take a look at 1D887 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, this is your evidence in the Tolimir case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we need page 67, which is transcript page 6884. Can we zoom in on lines 12 through 14, or rather, we just need line 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where you say, [In English] I quote: "I think that most of the people wanted to be evacuated." [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that most people, civilians, the people who remained in Srebrenica, wanted to be evacuated from Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: EVERT RAVE
